text:
alex_customer: Hey team — after the rollout last night our app started returning responses that drop the configured stop delimiter (we use `###`). Customers see the assistant keep generating and append extra stray tokens. Posting one example below.

alex_customer: REQUEST_ID: req_20240305_9876
alex_customer: model: redwood-3b-instruct (pinned)
alex_customer: stop: ["###"]
alex_customer: input (user prompt):
```
Write a short summary of the following policy:
- data retention is 90 days
- users can request deletion
```
alex_customer: output we get (truncated):
```
The policy states that data is retained for 90 days and users can request deletion. For deletion requests, the team... additional internal notes and references 0x02 0x7f etc
```

maya_cs: Thanks — sorry you're hitting this. Can you confirm whether this started immediately after the deploy? Did you see any errors in the API response (400/500) or is this purely a formatting/stop-token regression? :eyes:

alex_customer: It started right after the canary completed and full rollout. No HTTP errors — 200s with normal token counts but the trailing delimiter `###` missing and sometimes replaced with weird punctuation or extra words. Happens ~30% of requests.

deploy-bot: Deployment notice: release/v20240305 rolled out to default cluster at 2024-03-05T23:40:00Z by jess_eng — canary 2% for 4h then full.

jess_eng: I can repro locally with the customer's curl. Posting the exact request we ran: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-instruct","input":"Write a short summary of the following policy:\n- data retention is 90 days\n- users can request deletion\n","stop":["###"]}'
```

jess_eng: Response body we saw: 
```
{"id":"resp_abc","output":"The policy states that data is retained for 90 days and users can request deletion. For deletion requests, the team should contact support. Additional notes follow..."}
```

jess_eng: Note: there's no `###` at the end; previously the API appended the stop sequence and trimmed generation.

anish_ml: Hypothesis: stop-sequence post-processing path changed in runtime v2. The new kernel selection code touched tokenization/byte offsets for some models. Could be stop matching shifted from token-level to byte-level compare, failing when model emits different whitespace/soft-newline tokens.

anish_ml: Quick check — can you share the exact tokenization for the last tokens? (we can diff old vs new). If we see token-level mismatch, fallback to token-based stop matching is needed.

maya_cs: Customer would like ETA for fix or a rollback option — they're pretty sensitive to policy text formatting.

tom_infra: No infra outage or OOMs. The only infra change last night was the runtime bump (runtime-agent v2.1) that jess_eng mentioned. Latency profile stable.

jess_eng: I ran a token dump against the model using the same prompt: 
```
last_tokens: [" deletion", ".", " For", " deletion", " requests", " ,", " the", " team"]
```

jess_eng: Looks like the model emits a leading space token before the stop sequence; old postprocess stripped leading whitespace when matching `###` and then consumed it; new path seems stricter, so stop match fails and generation continues until an end-of-stream or other heuristics kick in.

anish_ml: That makes sense. Two action options: revert runtime v2.1 to restore old stop matching behavior, or patch postprocessing to normalize whitespace before stop matching (safer short-term).

maya_cs: Customer needs a short-term mitigation. Can we hotfix postprocessing to normalize whitespace for stop matching and do a quick canary?

jess_eng: I can ship a targeted hotfix to the stop-matcher in the hosted pipeline and run 5% canary for 30m. If green, promote. Will need infra assist for canary knobs.

tom_infra: I can open the canary and monitor. ETA ~40m to have canary running.

maya_cs: Thanks — I'll tell the customer we have a canary going and to expect updates. Please post the canary request IDs so I can correlate.

deploy-bot: Canary opened: canary_id=canary_20240305_stopfix at 2024-03-06T00:35:00Z (5%).

jess_eng: Pushed hotfix to stop-matcher. Initial canary checks look good — stop delimiter now appears on sampled responses. Rolling to 20% for extra sampling.

alex_customer: Thanks, seeing better results on our side too. We'll keep monitoring and will report if anything odd shows up.

maya_cs: Follow-ups: (1) anish to own root-cause postmortem (tokenization vs whitespace handling) (2) eng to put regression test in eval harness for stop sequences with whitespace variants (3) CS to notify affected customers with rollback notice if problems return.

anish_ml: On it — will post findings in #eng-ml and link a short writeup.

jess_eng: Marking thread resolved for now; will update if canary shows regressions while ramping. :white_check_mark:
